title: Functions: Linear Inequalities in Two Variables

findings.finding: Hold the boundary fixed while varying inequality direction and boundary inclusion.
findings.breakdown: The comparison separates which side to shade from whether the boundary is included.
findings.checked: The existing practice varies equations as well as inequality symbols; it contains no consecutive fixed-boundary comparison. All proposed sketches use methods taught on pages 4–6, and their stated answers are correct.

repair.proposal: After p7-q1-l, add the single instruction 'Predict what changes before each sketch.' Add further parts under the existing sketching instruction: (m) y > x + 4 [dotted; above]; (n) y < x + 4 [dotted; below]; (o) y ≤ x + 4 [solid; below]; (p) y ≥ x + 4 [solid; above]. Each boundary has intercepts (-4,0) and (0,4). The boundary stays fixed; each successive part changes either direction or inclusion. Follow with unpatterned part (q) y > 3 - 2x [dotted; above; intercepts (3/2,0) and (0,3)].

findings.doneWhen: The four fixed-boundary comparisons are followed by the unpatterned sketch.

findings.finding: The opening review omits algebraic isolation of a variable and signed substitution used directly in the introductory teaching.
findings.breakdown: The review's inequalities already have x isolated. Students then need to substitute negative coordinates in p4-pair-tests-node and isolate y in p5-example-stage1 while learning how inequalities define regions.
findings.checked: The complete teaching contains no earlier topic. The line-graph review rehearses intercepts but does not require substituting a negative coordinate. The positive-coefficient inequality in p4-solve-node occurs after the opening review. Negative division has been removed from this finding: it is not used in the worked example, and the guided-practice responses explicitly explain reversal.
findings.assumptions: Algebraic isolation and signed substitution are prior knowledge, consistent with the separate algebra and Inequalities booklets. No calculator is assumed.

repair.proposal: Append three compact items to the existing review, keeping the complete review within one page: (a) Solve 3u + 2 > 14 [u > 4]. (b) Make y the subject of 4y > 12 - 2x [y > 3 - x/2]. (c) For (x,y) = (-4,4), evaluate 2x - 3 and decide whether y ≥ 2x - 3 [-11; yes].

findings.doneWhen: The opening review checks positive-coefficient algebraic isolation and signed substitution before students use them to interpret graphical regions.

protectedGroups.observation: At the same x-coordinate, a point above the boundary satisfies the inequality and a point below it does not.
Shading unwanted half-planes and overlapping required half-planes identify the same intersection.
protectedGroups.varies: Which half-planes are shaded and how the final region is identified.

notReliablyReviewed.reason: Page images for these supplied graphs were not attached. Their described mathematical demands were reviewed from the specs; the visible coordinate and vertex labels could not be independently inspected.

importReview: Lean content review table: 29 of 29 blocks passed.

dropped.reason: The claimed missing pieces do not survive the opening-review test. p4-solve-node already rehearses isolating a variable by adding a term and dividing by a positive coefficient before p5-example-stage1, whose displayed rearrangement models moving the x-term. Negative-division reversal is needed in p5-guided-a, but no worked example requires it, so it cannot support this opening-review finding. No qualifying unrehearsed piece remains.

candidates.finding: The opening review asks students only to 'Sketch linear inequalities on a number line' in already-solved form, so it does not rehearse the algebraic rearrangement used in the worked graphing example or the negative-division reversal needed immediately afterwards.
